last_line: N: In the morning her chair stood at the Commander's right hand at the palace's long table. No servant admitted moving it. She had left her glass there, its rim marked with lipstick. The steward who tried to move it back found his fingers would not close on it. On the mirror, in lipstick, in a hand the Commander knew: "My favour. The chair at your right hand, at every table you will ever sit at. I have just collected the first night of it."

N: Nocticula took the Commander's hand before the glass reached the table.

default_text: {n}She took the Commander's hand and set it at her waist, holding their eyes with hers. "Yes," she said once more, against their mouth, and her breath caught, and the world ceased to exist.{/n}
